_about: Resorts within roughly 2 hours' drive of Salzburg city (Austria only). driveMin = approximate drive time from Salzburg in normal winter traffic, rounded estimates. forecastElev = metres used for the forecast (near the upper part of the ski area). exposure: north = northern ranges, favoured by Nordstau (NW/N flow); tauern = Hohe/Niedere Tauern main ridge, gets snow from north and south; inner = sheltered inner valleys, often miss Nordstau snow; south = south of the Tauern ridge, favoured by Suedstau (S/SW flow). freeride = 1-5 rating of off-piste/powder terrain. hype = 1-5 community/freeride reputation from rider guides and forums (researched Nov 2026, not live); says = paraphrased 'word on the street' with source.

resorts.name: Zwölferhorn – St. Gilgen
resorts.notes: Closest small area. Low elevation, so it only works when it is cold and the snow comes with a northern storm.

resorts.name: Gaissau-Hintersee
resorts.notes: First range south of the city, catches Nordstau well. Low top, so quality depends on temperature.

resorts.name: Werfenweng
resorts.notes: Under the Tennengebirge, which collects snow in northern flow.

resorts.name: Postalm
resorts.notes: Large alpine plateau, more a ski-touring classic than a powder resort. Good gentle terrain after a fresh dump.

resorts.name: Almenwelt Lofer
resorts.notes: Next to the Loferer Steinberge, which do well in northern storms.

resorts.name: Steinplatte – Waidring
resorts.notes: Northern rim of the Alps, gets the first hit of NW storms.

resorts.name: Snow Space Salzburg (Flachau/Wagrain/St. Johann)
resorts.notes: Big piste area; some tree and side-country lines between the lifts after fresh snow.

resorts.name: Dachstein West (Gosau/Annaberg/Russbach)
resorts.notes: North side of the Dachstein, catches northern flow. Low top, so watch the temperature.

resorts.name: Feuerkogel – Ebensee
resorts.notes: Plateau above the Traunsee, right at the northern edge of the Alps, so it gets a lot in Nordstau.

resorts.name: Hochkönig (Maria Alm/Dienten/Mühlbach)
resorts.notes: Hochkönig massif collects snow in northern storms. Hochkeil in Mühlbach is about 50 minutes from Salzburg.

says.text: On Salzburg guides' list of the best areas for freeriding.

resorts.name: Zauchensee / Flachauwinkl
resorts.notes: Higher base than its neighbours. The Schwarzwand has steep drops, trees and cliff lines for experts.

says.text: Powder chasers are told to check it out, between Obertauern and Snow Space.
On Salzburg guides' list of the best areas for freeriding.

resorts.name: Großarltal / Dorfgastein
resorts.notes: Inner valley: often gets little natural snow in Nordstau situations, better in westerly or southern flow.

resorts.name: Obertauern
resorts.notes: Snow-sure bowl with a 1,740 m base and a season from late November to early May. Freeride lines range from gentle near the Hundkogel to steep (Zehnerkar, Seekarspitze).

says.text: Named the snowiest spot in Salzburg state, and a Powderhounds favourite.
On Salzburg guides' list of the best areas for freeriding.

resorts.name: Dachstein Krippenstein (Obertraun)
resorts.notes: Freeride area with 30+ km of off-piste variants and 1,500 m of vertical. Mostly unprepared high-alpine terrain: go with a guide if you don't know it.

says.text: Described as a 'less frightening La Grave', with an 11 km top-to-bottom run.
Downside: the access cable cars fill up with non-skiing tourists, which hurts on powder days.

resorts.name: Fieberbrunn
resorts.notes: Known as a 'Schneeloch' (snow hole) because NW storms pile up here. Freeride World Tour venue (Wildseeloder). Part of Skicircus.

says.text: Cult freeride status; the Freeride World Tour has come here since 2011, and locals call it a 'Schneeloch' (snow hole).
Diverse freeride options plus its own snow and avalanche info system (LO.LA).

resorts.name: Saalbach Hinterglemm / Leogang
resorts.notes: Huge area, plenty of side-country between pistes on powder days. Same storms as Fieberbrunn, a bit less.

says.text: Skicircus is one of Powderhounds' favourite Austrian resorts; the best terrain spills into Tirol (Fieberbrunn side).

resorts.name: Schmittenhöhe – Zell am See
resorts.notes: Mostly piste. Useful backup when the Kitzsteinhorn is windy.

resorts.name: Planai / Schladming
resorts.notes: North side of the Niedere Tauern. Mostly piste.

resorts.name: Kitzsteinhorn – Kaprun
resorts.notes: Glacier, highest in the region, so it gets the coldest, driest snow. 'Freeride XXL' signposted routes with safety info at each start. Exposed to wind.

says.text: Among the Alps' top freeride spots: powder fields, cliffs, natural pipes and five signposted routes.

resorts.name: Kitzbühel
resorts.notes: Lots of terrain between runs. Lower and warmer than the Tauern resorts.

resorts.name: Rauris
resorts.notes: Quiet Tauern valley; fresh snow stays untracked longer than in the big areas.

resorts.name: Bad Gastein (Stubnerkogel/Graukogel)
resorts.notes: Steep terrain off the Stubnerkogel. Gets snow from both northern and southern storms.

says.text: The whole Gastein valley suits freeriders, with powder areas from Dorfgastein to Sportgastein.

resorts.name: Großeck-Speiereck (Lungau)
resorts.notes: South of the Tauern: often dry in Nordstau, but gets the snow in southern (Südstau) storms.

says.text: On Salzburg guides' list of the best areas for freeriding.

resorts.name: SkiWelt Wilder Kaiser
resorts.notes: Big but low. Only worth it when it is cold.

resorts.name: Katschberg
resorts.notes: Through the Tauern tunnel. Profits from southern storms when the north side stays dry.

resorts.name: Sportgastein
resorts.notes: Salzburg's highest glacier-free area (2,686 m), wide open slopes. Marked freeride routes: Golden Powder, Golden Rush, Golden Ride.

says.text: Grew from insider tip to freeride hotspot; wide, secluded slopes with an 'Alaska feeling'.

resorts.name: Hinterstoder
resorts.notes: Totes Gebirge area, gets heavy Nordstau snow.
